about-us.description: Erskine Electrical Solutions offers top-quality electrical services for residential repairs and commercial installations tailored to your needs.

text.text: We pride ourselves on delivering top-quality electrical services for projects of all sizes, from minor residential repairs to large-scale commercial installations. Dedicated to providing reliable, efficient, and safe solutions tailored to each client’s unique needs. Whether it’s a simple wiring fix, a full home rewire, or a complex industrial project, we approach every job with the same level of professionalism and attention to detail.

Fully certified in BS7671 Requirements for Electrical Installations, ensuring full compliance with all current wiring regulations. Additionally, we hold qualifications in BS7671 Periodic Inspection and Testing, enabling us to carry out thorough and accurate assessments of electrical systems. Our expertise extends to approved Health & Safety practices, ensuring all projects are completed in the safest manner possible. We are also certified in First Aid, PASMA (Prefabricated Access Suppliers’ and Manufacturers’ Association), and IPAF (International Powered Access Federation), demonstrating our commitment to safety and operational excellence across all types of electrical work.

At Erskine Electrical Solutions, we pride ourselves on delivering a professional, reliable service where safety and compliance are always the top priority. As a SELECT-registered electrical contractor, all work is carried out to the latest British Standards and Scottish regulations, ensuring every installation is safe, compliant, and built to last. We are fully insured for your peace of mind, and every job is completed with thorough testing, certification, and attention to detail. Our commitment to high standards means you can trust that all electrical work is completed correctly, safely, and with minimal disruption.

As a proud member of SELECT, the trade association for the electrical contracting industry in Scotland, we are committed to upholding the highest standards of professionalism, safety, and quality in all our work. SELECT membership provides us with access to ongoing training, technical support, and industry updates, ensuring we stay at the forefront of the latest developments and best practices in the electrical field. Membership also signifies our adherence to stringent codes of practice and a strong commitment to continuous improvement, giving our clients complete confidence in the reliability and excellence of our services.

The prices shown below are based on previous jobs our team has completed and are provided as a general guide only. We know that every project is different, with its own unique requirements and site conditions. To give a truly accurate quote, we always recommend a site visit so we can assess the work in detail. This page is designed to offer transparency and help our clients understand typical costs, while ensuring that all pricing is fair and tailored to each individual job.

Our standard call-out fee for domestic work is £100, which covers the electrician’s attendance and initial assessment for the first hour. After this, work is charged at £50 per hour for call-outs, general maintenance, and repairs.

Please note that prices may vary for out-of-hours work or Sunday visits. This structure ensures transparency, while allowing us to provide a fair and accurate price based on the specific work required.

Our pricing for Domestic EICRs typically ranges between £200 – £250. The exact price depends on property size and the number of circuits or consumer units. Larger properties with more wiring and electrical outlets take longer to test, so the price may be higher. Another factor that can affect pricing is the age and condition of the installation. Older, damaged, or deteriorating electrical systems may require a larger amount of sampling to produce a detailed and accurate report.
Up to 10 circuits £250 – £400 Small offices, shops, or retail units. Includes full EICR testing and certification.
11 – 20 circuits £400 – £650 -Medium offices, small warehouses, or larger retail spaces. Covers visual inspection, testing, and reporting.
21 – 40 circuits £650 – £1,000 - Larger offices, schools, or commercial premises. Multiple distribution boards may be included.
41 – 60 circuits £1,000 – £1,500 Multi-floor offices, industrial units, or large commercial sites. Complex systems and three-phase circuits may apply.
60+ circuits £1,500+ Large industrial, leisure, or multi-building sites. Price depends on site complexity, access, and number of boards.
Single Room / Minor Rewire £600 – £1100 Ideal for small kitchens, bathrooms, or single rooms. Includes sockets, lighting, and minor circuit work
.1–2 Bedroom Flat / House £2,500 – £3,500 Full rewire of small residential property, including new consumer unit, sockets, and lighting circuits.
3 Bedroom House £3,500 – £5,500 Standard full rewire, including consumer unit upgrade, lighting, sockets, and earthing/bonding.
4–5 Bedroom House £5,500 – £8,000 Larger properties with multiple floors and rooms; may include multiple consumer units or complex wiring.
Extensions / Renovations From £1,000 Additional work for home extensions or loft conversions; pricing varies depending on size and circuits.
Additional factors affecting price include access to walls/ceilings, number of sockets/lighting points and if property is occupied or not.
All work is tested, certified, and fully compliant with BS 7671 regulations.
Commercial rewires can vary greatly because every building and electrical system is unique. A site visit is always necessary to accurately assess the work and provide a fair, tailored quote.
Pricing can be affected by factors such as:

Building size and number of floors Number of circuits and distribution boards Three-phase vs single-phase supply Access and installation complexity (walls, ceilings, or hard-to-reach areas) Additional systems (lighting, emergency lighting, fire alarms, data cabling) Health & safety requirements and working hours Client-specific needs (phased work, special equipment)
A site visit allows us to assess all these factors, plan the work safely, and provide a transparent, accurate quote for your project.

All our consumer units are installed to the highest standards, ensuring both safety and reliability. Each unit is fully loaded with RCBOs to provide individual circuit protection, along with a Surge Protection Device (SPD) to safeguard your electrical system from voltage spikes. All installations are carried out in full compliance with current BS 7671 regulations, giving you peace of mind that your property’s electrical system is safe, fully compliant, and built to last.

Our minimum call-out fee is £100, which applies if PAT testing is the only work at the property. This covers travel, setup, and certification time. Additional appliances are charged at £3 per item. If we are already working on site, the first ten appliances are charged at £70, with £3 per item thereafter. This includes a visual inspection, electrical test, and a certificate issued upon completion.

Our emergency lighting tests are designed to ensure compliance with BS 5266-1 and BS EN 50172. Each test includes visual inspections, functional checks, battery discharge tests, and certification. Prices are indicative, as every site is unique. A site visit is always recommended for an accurate quotation.
Small sites (up to ~10 lights)£200 – £250 Standard 3-hour test, includes certification. Covers offices, small shops, or residential blocks.
Medium sites (10 – 40 lights) £250 – £400 Includes multiple floors or larger layouts. Price may vary depending on access and number of circuits.
Large sites (40+ lights) £400 – £700+ Multi-floor offices, hotels, industrial units, or large retail spaces. May require multiple visits.
Domestic Smoke and Heat Alarm installation

As an Aico Approved Installer, we only supply and install fully compliant smoke, heat, and carbon monoxide alarms, meeting current Scottish legislation. All alarms are correctly sited, interlinked, tested, commissioned and certified ensuring your property is safe, compliant, and future-proof.
Individual Alarm Replacement / Upgrade Prices from £150 Like-for-like replacement or upgrade of existing compliant alarms.
Full interlinked battery system - Standard 2 story dwelling - £430
Prices below indicative for a fully hard wired new installation
1 Bedroom Flat £300 – £450 Smoke, heat, and CO alarms installed to current standards, fully interlinked and tested.
2 Bedroom Flat / House £450 – £600 Full compliant system including required alarm coverage and commissioning.
3 Bedroom House £600 – £800 Multi-alarm system covering circulation spaces, living areas, and kitchens as required.
4–5 Bedroom House £800 – £1,100 Larger properties with additional alarms and interlinking.

Electrical installation work, ranging from full property rewires to targeted upgrades for kitchens and bathrooms. Every project, whether it's modernizing an entire home or enhancing specific areas like kitchens and bathrooms, meets the highest standards of safety and functionality. With meticulous attention to detail, we manage all aspects of the installation process, including wiring, lighting, and appliance connections, ensuring seamless integration and optimal performance. Trust us to deliver reliable, efficient, and tailored electrical solutions that enhance the comfort and value of your property.

In the UK, Electrical Installation Condition Reports (EICRs) are produced to ensure the safety, efficiency, and compliance of electrical installations within properties. These reports are crucial for identifying any potential hazards, defects, or non-compliances with current regulations, thereby preventing electrical accidents and fires. Regular EICR inspections help property owners and landlords adhere to legal safety standards, protect occupants, and maintain the integrity of the electrical systems. By providing a comprehensive assessment of an installation's condition, EICRs play a vital role in safeguarding both people and property, promoting a safer living and working environment.

Undertaking consumer unit upgrades to enhance electrical safety, comply with current BS7671 regulations , and accommodate increased electrical demands. Upgrading the consumer unit ensures that circuits are adequately protected against overload and fault conditions, reducing the risk of electrical fires and ensuring the system can safely handle modern appliances and technologies. Additionally, it may be necessary to meet insurance requirements or before selling a property, demonstrating compliance and ensuring the electrical system is reliable and up to date.
Precise and efficient electrical fault finding services to quickly identify and resolve issues in your systems.
Undertaking all types of general electrical installation work, delivering high-quality solutions for projects of any size.
Providing reliable electrical maintenance services and swift call-outs, ensuring your systems remain safe and operational at all times.

We provide smoke and heat alarm installation and certification to ensure the safety and well-being of residents. These installations are crucial in meeting legal requirements and enhancing fire safety standards within homes and properties. By providing this service, we aim to protect lives and properties from the devastating effects of fires, promoting peace of mind and compliance with regulatory standards across Scotland.
PAT testing for landlords and commercial properties, carried out by a qualified electrician. Fast, reliable testing with clear certification to keep your property safe and compliant.

blocks.text: Welcome to "A Day in the Life"... Of an Electrician.

Hello and welcome,  I'm excited to take you on a journey through my world of electrical work, sharing the ins and outs of what it means to be an electrician. Whether you are simply curious about what we do or  already a fellow tradesperson, then this blog is for you.

Let me introduce myself. My name is Keir, and I've been working as an electrician for over 11 years. Over time, I've tackled a wide variety of electrical projects, from residential installations and commercial wiring to fault finding complex systems. Working in a number of environments from airports, hospitals, high schools to domestic dwellings allowing me to accumulate a wide range of knowledge over the years.
In this blog, I'll be sharing my day-in day-out experiences, challenges, and triumphs on the job. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect:
Regular Logs: Detailed accounts of my day-to-day tasks, including the different types of jobs I handle, the tools and techniques I use, and how I solve unexpected problems.

Project Highlights: In-depth looks at some of the more interesting projects I work on and even some of the minor works. You'll get a behind-the-scenes look at how these projects come together from start to finish.
Industry Insights: Updates on the latest trends and technologies in the electrical industry and how these advancements are shaping our work and what the future might hold.

Tips and Tricks: Practical advice and insights for aspiring electricians and DIY enthusiasts. From safety protocols to efficiency hacks covering a range of topics. Who knows? You might actually learn something new!
Q&A Sessions: Opportunities for you to ask questions and get answers. Whether you're curious about a specific aspect of electrical work or need advice on a project you're tackling.

Being an electrician is a profession that requires a unique blend of technical knowledge, problem-solving skills, and hands-on expertise. By sharing my experiences, I hope to inspire others to appreciate the art and science behind electrical work.
Thank you for visiting, I look forward to sharing my journey with you and hope you find this blog both informative and enjoyable.
